name: Exercise.com
description: Exercise.com gym and coaching software: members and staff, appointments and classes, scheduled occurrences and rosters, visits and check-ins, calendar, services, locations, availability schedules, waitlists, assessments, groups and group calendars, purchases, appointment packages and logged workouts with per-exercise history. Tenant API v4 on your own platform host.
instructions:
**Credentials**: Exercise.com runs each business on its own host (your custom-branded platform, e.g. `train.yourgym.com` or `yourgym.exercise.com`). Put that host, without https://, in `EXERCISE_HOST`; the API is served from it at `/api/v4`.

API access is a paid add-on: ask your Exercise.com account representative to enable it. The v4 API takes two credentials on each call, as its reference documents (security `api_key` and `bearer` together):
1. `EXERCISE_API_KEY`: create it under **Account > Customize Platform > Developers > Add** and copy it at once (it is shown only once). Sent in the `API-TOKEN` header.
2. `EXERCISE_ACCESS_TOKEN`: the bearer token of the account the API acts as (a Personal API Token issued in the product, or the token provided with API access), sent as `Authorization: Bearer`. Use a token of the owner or an admin to see every member.
Most member, booking and service reads answer with the access token alone, but schedules, assessment templates and logged workouts answer 401 unless both are sent.

**Where to start**: `exercise_com_list_users` gives member and staff ids (`user_id`). For bookings use `exercise_com_get_calendar` with `affinity=schedule` and a Unix-time window, or `exercise_com_list_appointments` / `exercise_com_list_scheduled_appointments`, then `exercise_com_list_visits` with `appointment_id` for who booked and attended.

**Tools by area**:
- Members and staff: `exercise_com_list_users`, `exercise_com_get_user`, `exercise_com_list_purchased_items` (what a member bought and how they pay).
- Bookings: `exercise_com_list_appointments`, `exercise_com_get_appointment`, `exercise_com_list_appointment_packages` (packages that pay for an appointment), `exercise_com_list_scheduled_appointments`, `exercise_com_get_scheduled_appointment`, `exercise_com_list_scheduled_appointment_members` (rosters; `for_user` for one member), `exercise_com_list_visits` (`for_user` for one member's bookings), `exercise_com_get_visit`, `exercise_com_list_waitlist_entries`, `exercise_com_get_calendar`.
- Setup: `exercise_com_list_services`, `exercise_com_get_service`, `exercise_com_list_locations`, `exercise_com_list_schedules`, `exercise_com_list_groups`, `exercise_com_list_group_calendars`.
- Assessments: `exercise_com_list_assessments`, `exercise_com_get_assessment` (template with its questions), `exercise_com_list_user_assessments`, `exercise_com_get_user_assessment` (a member's answers).
- Training: `exercise_com_list_workouts`, `exercise_com_list_user_workout_exercises` (a member's logged sets per exercise over time).
- Writes: `exercise_com_book_visit` books a member into an appointment, `exercise_com_cancel_visit` cancels a booking; confirm with the user first.

**Filtering**: most list tools take `filter`, Ransack predicates written as a query-string fragment: `q[status_eq]=completed&q[created_at_gteq]=2026-09-01`. Keys are `<field>_<predicate>` such as `_eq`, `_in`, `_gteq`, `_lteq`, `_cont`; `q[s]=created_at desc` sorts. Unknown fields are ignored or rejected depending on the resource, so start without a filter and look at the field names in the answer.

**Appointments need a date window**: `exercise_com_list_appointments` over the whole history is slow enough to fail with HTTP 500, so its `filter` is required; pass `q[start_time_gteq]` and `q[start_time_lt]`.

**Paging**: `per` and `page` (from 1). When either is set, the answer includes `meta.total`. Without them some lists return everything. `pluck_columns` returns a plain array of just those stored columns for every match (it can ignore `per`), handy for id lookups; computed fields such as `service_name` are not columns and make the call fail.

**Times**: the calendar takes Unix timestamps in seconds for `start` and `end`; other filters take dates or ISO 8601 times. Visits carry the time zone of the business.

**Errors**: 401 `Access denied` means a wrong host, a wrong or revoked token, or API access not enabled; 403 means the token's account may not see the resource; 404 a wrong id.

The interactive reference is at https://train.demoexercise.com/api-docs/ ("API V4 Docs"); its login is given in Exercise.com's support article on API keys (the docsUrl of this connector).

A member's package balances (credits left), invoices and charges are not part of the documented v4 tenant API, so this connector does not read them; `exercise_com_list_purchased_items` shows what was bought and `exercise_com_list_appointment_packages` which packages fit an appointment.
prerequisites: API access is a paid add-on of Exercise.com: your account representative enables it. You need an API key from **Account > Customize Platform > Developers** and an access token of the owner or an admin account.

EXERCISE_HOST.label: Platform host
EXERCISE_HOST.help: The host name your members and staff open the platform at, without https:// and without a path, e.g. train.yourgym.com.
EXERCISE_HOST.patternMessage: Only the host name, e.g. train.yourgym.com, without https:// or a path.

EXERCISE_API_KEY.label: API key
EXERCISE_API_KEY.help: Account > Customize Platform > Developers > Add. Copy it right away; Exercise.com shows it only once. Sent in the API-TOKEN header.

EXERCISE_ACCESS_TOKEN.label: Access token
EXERCISE_ACCESS_TOKEN.help: The bearer token of the account the API acts as: a Personal API Token issued in the product, or the access token your account representative provides with API access. Paste it without the word Bearer.

verifyHints.401: Exercise.com answered "Access denied". Check the host is your own platform host, that both the API key (Developers tab) and the access token are current, and that API access is enabled for your account.
verifyHints.403: The credentials work but the account may not read this. Use an access token of the platform owner or an admin.
verifyHints.unreachable: Nothing answered at this host. Enter only the host name you open the platform at, e.g. train.yourgym.com.

tools.name: exercise_com_list_users
tools.description: List the platform's users (members, clients and staff) with name, e-mail, phone, head trainer and sign-up dates. Filter with q[email_cont]=... or trainer_id; the id is the user_id other tools use.

trainer_id.description: Only users whose head trainer is this user id.

with_ids.description: Comma-separated user ids to fetch; paging is ignored when set.

filter.description: Ransack filter as a query-string fragment of q[...] predicates joined with &, e.g. q[status_eq]=completed&q[created_at_gteq]=2026-09-01. Predicates: _eq, _not_eq, _in, _lt, _lteq, _gt, _gteq, _cont, _null; q[s]=created_at desc sorts.

pluck_columns.description: Comma-separated stored columns to return instead of full records, e.g. id,first_name,last_name,email. The answer is then a plain array of every match (per and page may be ignored); computed fields such as service_name are not columns and fail.

per.description: Records per page. When per or page is set the answer carries meta.total with the total count.

tools.name: exercise_com_get_user
tools.description: Return one user by id with profile, contact details, head trainer, membership and sign-up information.

tools.name: exercise_com_list_visits
tools.description: List visits (bookings and check-ins of a member for an appointment or class) with status, registered, completed, no-show and cancelled times, payment and package used. Filter by appointment, by member (for_user), by ids or with a Ransack filter.

appointment_id.description: Only visits of this appointment id.

active_visits.description: Pass true to return only finished visits for appointments and check-ins.

for_user.description: A user id: only the visits that user can access (their own bookings and check-ins).

with_ids.description: Comma-separated visit ids to fetch; paging is ignored when set.

tools.name: exercise_com_get_calendar
tools.description: Return calendar events between two Unix timestamps: appointments and trainer availability (affinity schedule), scheduled workouts (logger), logged workouts (summary) or assessments, habits and check-ins (webview).

start.description: Window start as a Unix timestamp in seconds, e.g. 1759708800.

end.description: Window end as a Unix timestamp in seconds.

affinity.description: Comma-separated: schedule (appointments and availability), logger (scheduled workouts), summary (logged workouts), webview (assessments, habits, check-ins, waivers). affinity or object_type is required.

object_type.description: Comma-separated object types instead of affinity: appointment, scheduled_appointment, schedule, schedule_service, workout, logged-workout, assessment, habit, checkin, required.

service_id.description: schedule affinity: only this service id.

trainer_id.description: schedule affinity: only this trainer's user id.

location_id.description: schedule affinity: only this location id.

cancelled.description: schedule affinity: true to include cancelled events.

tools.name: exercise_com_list_user_workout_exercises
tools.description: Return a member's logged history of workout exercises (sets, reps, weights), oldest first, paginated. Pass exercise_id for one exercise's progress, with_date=true to include the workout date (it lives on the workout, not the exercise), and pluck_columns to keep answers small.

exercise_id.description: Only the history of this exercise.

with_date.description: true to include the date of the workout each exercise belongs to.

sort.description: Sort order sent as q[s]; workout_workout_date desc returns the newest first.

pluck_columns.description: Comma-separated stored columns to return instead of full records, e.g. id,first_name,last_name,email. The answer is then a plain array of every match (per and page may be ignored); computed fields such as service_name are not columns and fail.

tools.name: exercise_com_list_purchased_items
tools.description: List what a member has bought: per item its type and id (package, workout plan, group...) and the payment option used (purchase or subscription, amount, currency, interval).

user_id.description: Member's user id from exercise_com_list_users; without it the API answers for the user the access token belongs to.

tools.name: exercise_com_book_visit
tools.description: Book a member into an appointment by creating a visit. Booking can charge the member or use one of their packages, depending on the service settings.

tools.name: exercise_com_cancel_visit
tools.description: Delete (cancel) a visit by id. Late-cancel rules and fees of the service may apply, and the member may be notified.
